content: Luliconazole is an antifungal agent classified under the azole group. It is formulated as a white cream for topical application, marketed under the brand name LUZU. The cream contains 1% luliconazole, which corresponds to 10 mg of the active ingredient per gram of cream. Chemically, luliconazole is identified as (2E)-2-(2-imidazol-1-yl)acetonitrile. It is the R-enantiomer, meaning it has a specific three-dimensional configuration, and it possesses one chiral center. Additionally, the double bond adjacent to the dithiolane group in its structure is in the E configuration, indicating the spatial arrangement of the substituents around the double bond. The formulation of LUZU Cream, 1%, includes a vehicle composed of several excipients. These include benzyl alcohol, butylated hydroxytoluene, cetostearyl alcohol, isopropyl myristate, medium-chain triglycerides, methylparaben, polysorbate 60, propylene glycol, purified water, and sorbitan monostearate. These components serve various roles, such as stabilizing the formulation, enhancing absorption, and preserving the product.
